rationale: ROUND 2, answering round 1's gating objection. Round 1 shipped a SHAPE rule: a recombination tail segment was admitted as 'English' if it was digit-free, >=2 characters and lower-case. The compliance seat rejected that at HIGH severity and was right — shape is orthographic, not semantic, so 'not', 'instead', 'unless', 'lower' pass exactly the same test as 'or' and 'better'. 'IP54-not-rated' would have cleared a gate whose whole purpose is to stop a customer-facing report asserting something the facts do not say; the fabrication simply moved from the model number to the qualifier. The edit-quality seat named the same hole from the other end (spelled-out numerals: '2F-eighty-five' is lower-case English too), and separately objected that the round-1 rationale claimed three independently mutation-tested clauses while the code implemented digit-rejection and case-rejection as ONE character-range check — one line absorbing two claimed clauses. Both are accepted in full. The shape rule is GONE, replaced by a closed vocabulary: a tail segment must be a member of qualifierWords, compared case-insensitively. Admission has two rules and everything absent is absent on purpose: CONNECTIVES that assert nothing (and, of, or, to) and RESTATEMENTS of the stated value — 'meets what the fact block says' (rated, compliant, compatible, class) or 'at least as much as it says' (better, above, minimum). No negation, no inversion, no numeral words. The unchanged part of the case still stands and was re-verified: exactly ONE active non-snapshot agent definition contains this action (report-builder), the two existing clearance routes are untouched and tried first, and fail-closed is untouched. Base defect unchanged: 1 of 2 retained report orchestrations died on 'summary_html names model-like token "IP54-or-better"' with IP54 present in the fact block, and its URL 404s.

plan.summary: Round 2 replaces the tail rule and nothing else. qualifierSegment is now a single case-insensitive membership test against a closed vocabulary (qualifierWords); the digit / length / lower-case clauses are deleted rather than supplemented, because a shape rule cannot distinguish a connective from a negation. Case-insensitivity also retires round 1's first disclosed residual: 'IP54-Rated' in a heading now clears, since the vocabulary and not the capitalisation carries the safety property. skuTokenTraces, the call site, the two existing routes and fail-closed are exactly as reviewed in round 1.

edits.rationale: The closed vocabulary the compliance seat asked for, with its admission rules written beside it and the round-1 verdict cited as the reason it exists. Answers the HIGH objection directly: 'not', 'non', 'without', 'unless', 'instead', 'under', 'below', 'less', 'lower' and every numeral word are absent, so a tail can restate or strengthen a published figure but can never invert or replace one. Also answers edit-quality's second objection, which is the same hole entered from the numeral side. The stated cost is accepted and written into the comment: a legitimate qualifier not on the list costs ONE rejected report, which the writer usually clears on retry with different phrasing, and extending the list is a one-line change plus a test — whereas a shape rule ships a report that contradicts the specification it cites.

edits.rationale: Answers edit-quality's first objection structurally rather than by rewording the claim: there is no longer a conjunction of clauses for one line to absorb, only a membership test, and what is now mutation-pinned is each individual EXCLUSION from the vocabulary. Case-insensitive comparison is deliberate — it retires round 1's title-case residual, and the capitalisation of a word was never what made it safe.

Answers compliance's second objection: the round-1 table tested only invented SIBLING CODES, so it could not have caught the qualifier hole and a reviewer reading green tests would have concluded the gate was safe. Three meaning-inverting cases added, each constructed so that every OTHER segment in its tail is admitted — so the case fails on exactly one word and admitting that word to the vocabulary flips it. 'IP54-not-rated' is the one-segment negation of the legitimate 'IP54-rated'. Mutation matrix, all four re-run on the final code: vocabulary -> the round-1 shape rule fails all three semantic cases; admitting 'not' fails IP54-not-rated ALONE; admitting 'lower' fails IP54-or-lower ALONE; disabling route 3 fails the accept test. The sibling-code cases (2F-140, 2F-85-XL, 2F-85-x, GEP5010IO-00-B) are retained unchanged.

Answers edit-quality's low objection by showing the accept side in full: it asserts BOTH that no violation mentions 'model-like token' AND that len(v)==0, the first because the numeric gate at :307 rejects many of the same strings for a different reason and would otherwise absorb a mutation of the SKU rule (the landmine recorded 2026-07-31). One case added for the retired title-case residual.

grounded_in: round-1 gating objection, compliance, HIGH: 'qualifierSegment accepts ANY all-lowercase alphabetic segment length>=2 as a safe English qualifier with no closed vocabulary. This is orthographic, not semantic... A tail like IP54-instead-of-ip65 or IP54-not-required clears route 3 while asserting the OPPOSITE of what buildFactBlock stated.'

round-1 objection, editquality, medium: 'the sketch's qualifierSegment implements digit-rejection and case-rejection as ONE character-range check. A single mutation to that line flips both claims at once.'

round-1 objection, editquality, medium: 'This also clears spelled-out numeral words (e.g. a tail like eighty-five), which is exactly the fabricated-sibling-model-number class the guard exists to stop.'

DISCLOSURE — the round-1 test suite would not have caught the widening even after the semantic cases were added: TestProseGateStillRejectsFabricatedSiblings ran at ipMin 0, and buildFactBlock (score_grippers_action.go:737-739) only writes 'required protection IP%d' when IPMin > 0. So every IP54-* case was rejected for an untraceable HEAD and never reached the tail rule at all — mutations that admitted 'not' and 'lower' both passed. Found by running the mutations, not by reading the test. The fixture is now ipMin 54 and each mutation fails on exactly its own case.
